_note: Under-explored concepts shaped for the channel. Scientific bounds, sources, counterviews, and blind spots live in evidence.json. A concept remains a candidate after use; novelty is calculated from the corpus and brief history.

frontier.title: Your Feelings Are Forecasts
frontier.science: One influential theory models emotion categories as learned inferences that integrate bodily signals, context, and prediction.
frontier.hook: What if the name your mind gives a body sensation is part report, part prediction?
frontier.metaphor: Emotions as weather forecasts made from bodily and contextual data.
frontier.turn: A forecast can be examined without pretending the weather is imaginary or freely controllable.
frontier.invitation: At the next strong feeling, ask: what signals and expectations might be shaping this interpretation?

frontier.title: You Don't Always Know Why You Did That
frontier.science: Choice-blindness experiments show that, under bounded conditions, people can explain an outcome that does not match the choice they made.
frontier.hook: There may be a press secretary in your head who sometimes learns the decision after the meeting.
frontier.metaphor: The interpreter as a spokesperson issuing a confident account from incomplete notes.
frontier.turn: Not knowing every cause is not failure; it is an opening for better questions.
frontier.invitation: Catch one reason you give today and ask: what evidence would distinguish motive from explanation?

frontier.title: Expectation Has Biological Consequences
frontier.science: Treatment context and expectation can alter some symptoms; open-label placebo has shown benefits in specific randomized trials.
frontier.hook: A treatment can change experience even when the patient knows it contains no active drug.
frontier.metaphor: Expectation as one signal among many in the body's control room.
frontier.turn: Beliefs can matter without becoming magic or replacing medical care.
frontier.invitation: Which expectation are you treating as harmless, and what measurable effect would reveal its influence?

frontier.title: You Meet Through a Model
frontier.science: Mentalizing research studies how people infer others' beliefs, intentions, and traits from incomplete information.
frontier.hook: The person in front of you and your model of them arrive together—but they are not identical.
frontier.metaphor: Every relationship includes a live reconstruction made from limited footage.
frontier.turn: The model is constrained by another real person who can surprise and correct it.
frontier.invitation: Picture someone you resent. Which parts are observations, and which parts are your reconstruction?

frontier.title: Memory Helps Build Tomorrow
frontier.science: Hippocampal systems contribute to both episodic recollection and construction of imagined experiences.
frontier.hook: Some of the machinery that remembers childhood also helps imagine next Tuesday.
frontier.metaphor: Memory as raw footage that can be re-cut into possible futures.
frontier.turn: The past supplies material, not a command for what must come next.
frontier.invitation: What piece of your past are you using as set dressing for a future you do not want?

frontier.title: When the Familiar Goes Alien
frontier.science: Laboratory repetition can make familiar words feel temporarily strange, a form of word alienation resembling jamais vu.
frontier.hook: Repeat an ordinary word until familiarity loosens and the letters look borrowed.
frontier.metaphor: The mind's familiar stamp wearing thin.
frontier.turn: Strangeness can renew attention without proving that an unfiltered reality has appeared.
frontier.invitation: Which ordinary object can you examine long enough to notice what familiarity normally hides?

frontier.title: The Continuity Editor
frontier.science: Change-blindness experiments show that people can miss large visual changes when continuity is interrupted.
frontier.hook: A scene can change in front of you while experience keeps insisting it was continuous.
frontier.metaphor: A film editor hiding cuts while attention protects the story.
frontier.turn: The useful question is not whether perception is fake, but what it preserves and what it drops.
frontier.invitation: Where have you accepted a smooth account that may have been assembled from discontinuous pieces?

frontier.title: Not Everyone Imagines the Same Way
frontier.science: Research documents stable differences in voluntary visual imagery, including aphantasia and hyperphantasia.
frontier.hook: Some people cannot voluntarily picture an apple; others experience an image with striking clarity.
frontier.metaphor: Different inner workspaces with different default tools—not better and worse machines.
frontier.turn: Your inner experience is one human variation, not the template for everyone.
frontier.invitation: Ask someone close what happens when they picture a beach, and listen without translating it into your experience.

frontier.title: Action Can Compress Felt Time
frontier.science: Intentional-binding tasks find that voluntary actions and their effects can be judged as temporally closer than control events.
frontier.hook: Cause and effect can feel closer when the action is yours.
frontier.metaphor: Agency as a small gravity well in experienced time.
frontier.turn: A laboratory timing judgment is not proof that action always creates flow or control.
frontier.invitation: Where does doing change your sense of waiting—and where does it not?

frontier.title: The Settings Menu Behind the Trip
frontier.science: The entropic-brain framework relates expansive conscious states to changes in measures of neural signal diversity.
frontier.hook: A psychedelic state may change the diversity and predictability of brain activity, not simply reveal a hidden world.
frontier.metaphor: The noise-cancelling settings change, and a different organization of the room becomes audible.
frontier.turn: Entropy is a model and measurement family, not a synonym for truth or raw signal.
frontier.invitation: When has experience become unusually expansive, and which explanations fit without outrunning the evidence?
frontier.note: DMT lane. Adverse experiences, set and setting, and grounding belong in the script. Do not generalize psychedelic findings to grief or meditation without separate sources.

frontier.title: The Edge of You Is Flexible
frontier.science: Synchronous sensory evidence can induce ownership of a rubber hand; tool use can also change aspects of body and near-space representation.
frontier.hook: Your brain can sometimes be persuaded that a rubber hand belongs to the body. What does that reveal—and what does it not?
frontier.metaphor: The body's working border as a chalk line revised by evidence.
frontier.turn: Flexibility does not mean unlimited conscious control; tools, close others, and grief require their own evidence and labels.
frontier.invitation: What have you called 'not me' without examining whether the boundary is sensory, social, practical, or metaphorical?

frontier.title: The Center of Narrative Gravity
frontier.science: Dennett's center of narrative gravity is a philosophical model, not an experimental discovery of an empty point in the brain.
frontier.hook: A center of gravity has real effects even though no little object sits at the coordinate.
frontier.metaphor: The narrative self as a center of gravity organizing a life story.
frontier.turn: A useful abstraction can be real in its consequences without being a permanent inner object.
frontier.invitation: Which parts of your identity are embodied, relational, remembered, or narrated—and what changes when you separate them?
